question: How are Adelaar's (1981) Batak reconstruction and correspondences entered beside Billings & McDonnell (2024)?
chosen_reading: Billings & McDonnell's nodes stay (pnb = Adelaar's Proto-Northern-Batak; pcsb = his Proto-Southern-Batak with Simalungun; psb = his Proto-Toba; his Proto-Angkola-Mandailing is not entered, as their AM-Batak is not). Adelaar's dialect correspondences are composed onto the node that all daughters showing them share, as a second source beside Billings & McDonnell's rows; new are *t > NB c before i and the loss of intervocalic *w in SB. His dialect inventories go in for Dairi, Toba, Angkola, Mandailing and Simalungun (Karo keeps Woollams 2005); Toba and Angkola (h) is an allophone of /k/. Simalungun j is Adelaar's voiced palatal stop ɟ, so Billings & McDonnell's sporadic Simalungun d͡ʒ shows as a reflex outside the inventory. Part III (PAN > PB) is not entered: Billings & McDonnell already state PSUM > PB, and Adelaar's PAN (Dyen's) does not map onto PMP one to one (*Z > PB *d beside *z > PB *j).
alternatives: Rename the nodes after Adelaar (Proto-Southern-Batak for pcsb, Proto-Toba for psb); add Proto-Angkola-Mandailing; enter Part III as PB rows against PSUM.
